item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00208","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C11","C22","C15"],"selected_candidate_label":"C11","confidence":0.84,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C11 plausibly supplied a material template for presenting a presidential water-resources policy report. Both letters explain that the report addresses basic national policy rather than isolated projects, frame Federal responsibilities alongside State, local, and private participation, discuss coordination and the balance between Federal leadership and local roles, and urge governmental consideration of the report. C22 is closely connected to the child’s subject and committee, but it is principally the committee-establishment directive rather than a report-transmittal template. C15 contains similar policy themes but is more remote in function.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"The policies set out in the report embody a framework within which the Federal Government, with state and local governments and other non-Federal interests, may cooperate to develop our water resources.","parent_excerpt":"accomplishment of this objective requires the combined efforts of Federal, State and local governments, as well as private interests","explanation":"Distinctively parallel enumeration of the governmental levels and private interests whose coordinated participation is required for water-resource development."},{"child_excerpt":"The report recognizes fully the responsibilities of the Federal Government for leadership, guidance and action in this field. At the same time, it recognizes that there are a multitude of water developments which are more appropriate for regional, state or local activity.","parent_excerpt":"the problem of striking an appropriate balance in achieving both a local voice in these matters and responsible administration of those functions which are properly the role of the Federal Government","explanation":"Both report letters use the same substantive framework: defining the proper balance between Federal responsibility and regional or local authority."},{"child_excerpt":"The report is the result of a detailed study of our water problems and of the present powers and activities of the various Federal establishments engaged in water resource development.","parent_excerpt":"The report thus concerns basic policies underlying the Federal Government's responsibilities in this field, rather than recommendations for or against specific projects.","explanation":"Both characterize a water-resources commission report as a broad review of Federal policy and institutional responsibilities, not merely a collection of project proposals."}]}
